messages.subject: proportional and additive error
parts:
Hi,

I am curious how to parametrize error model for PK problems where additive error prevails when concentrations are low and proportional error dominates when concentrations are high. I am getting a funnel for those error components when using stan's statement log concentration~normal(mu,sqrt(sigma_add^2+mu^2*sigma_prop^2). I assume that because of this I have divergent transitions.


Thanks for the insight how to deal with this. One way is to ignore additive component. I don't know how good this assumption is...

Linas

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] proportional and additive error
parts:
I've encountered this situation from time to time over the years.  One thing that sometimes works is a parameterization of the form, sd = sigma*(E(y)/Z)^alpha, where A is a constant set so that the thing inside the exponent is of order 1, and alpha is restricted to (0,1).  Another thing is to try modeling everything on the log scale.  Another tip is to use informative priors for the sigmas.  Another tip is to set up the parameterization so the sigmas are on unit scale.  In your example you can replace mu^2 by (mu/A)^2.

Hey, I guess this should go into the priors wiki!

A
